summary: 48 kHz DAC update and four-pole 20 kHz filter leave a 20 kHz tone's first image near -11.49 dBc.
description: Targeted SPICE of all four output filter paths gives -2.98768 dB at 20 kHz and -11.5574 dB at 28 kHz. With an ideal zero-order-hold DAC updated at 48 kHz and no digital interpolation, the image at 48-20=28 kHz is -11.4923 dBc relative to the wanted tone. A high-rejection audio reconstruction response is not established by the present four-pole cutoff check.
recommendation: Specify required reconstruction-image rejection. Reconcile DAC oversampling/digital interpolation or a more selective analog filter with the SPI/DMA budget, then simulate and bench-test the final chain.

computation.description: ngspice-46 simulation of the populated two-stage Sallen-Key networks, plus ideal zero-order-hold image/fundamental amplitude ratio.
computation.result: DAC 48 kHz, 20 kHz tone: first 28 kHz image -11.4923 dBc including ideal ZOH and analog filter.

summary: External input filter provides 43.54 dB relative rejection of 76 kHz interference that aliases to 20 kHz at 96 kHz sampling.
description: Targeted ideal SPICE of the populated input filters, 1 kohm input resistance, assumed 10 ohm ADG on-resistance, 47 ohm ADC series resistor, 100 pF cap and 1 Mohm ADC input gives -3.40254 dB at 20 kHz and -46.945 dB at 76 kHz. The external analog filter's relative rejection is 43.54246 dB. Digital decimation cannot undo an alias already generated by the ADC. The ADC's internal filter and actual source spectrum must be included before setting an end-to-end rejection claim.
recommendation: Specify maximum out-of-band input spectrum and acceptable alias level. Include the ADC internal analog bandwidth and the final digital decimator in the error budget; tighten analog filtering or raise ADC rate if the budget demands it.

computation.description: ngspice-46 complete input-path AC response, comparing a 76 kHz interferer and its 20 kHz alias at the planned 96 kHz sampling rate.
computation.result: ADC 96 kHz: external-filter rejection of 76 kHz aliased onto 20 kHz is -43.5425 dB relative to 20 kHz gain.
